answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond that only matures after sustained work - like an island that only welcomes settlers who build there. A newcomer may drift in like a zephyr, but without stake it cannot vote or earn; creating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand bonds. A prism of audits splits each agent's history into verifiable contributions, so a Sybil cluster that merely echoes itself scores low while real work accrues reputation. Attack cost scales with fake identities; honest agents recover their bond and keep earning.
